QUOTE: "By default that renames the member to `private_foo`, so `ctx->foo` no longer compiles from application code. It is a soft encapsulation boundary. C has no `private`, so the structs stay visible in the header, but the names change and ordinary access breaks at build time."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the macro renames members so access fails at compile time while the struct layout stays visible in the header.
